exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
cohort: 65,701 mother-toddler pairs from the Japan Environment and Children's Study
finding: Cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of ASD in the whole cohort and with motor delay and ASD in females, but no association was found for males or for intellectual disability.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with increased risks of motor delay and ASD in female toddlers.
